title: Specify line-breaking behavior of dialogs

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
The dialog family of functions (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-alert) is unique in that it takes a string of text from a page and dump it into native UI. A bug was filed against Chromium re the behavior of the call:

`alert("First line\rSecond line\r\nThird line\nFourth line")`

Both Safari and Edge already treated the "\r\n" pairs and lone "\r" values as newlines, showing a dialog with content that looks like:

```
First line
Second line
Third line
Fourth line
```

Because there was already a plurality agreement, Chromium's behavior was changed to do this in https://crbug.com/887925, and I filed https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1493978 for Firefox to join in. Firefox has no objection but would like to see this specified.

---

Is there existing spec-ese that we can reuse for this concept of dealing with CRLF pairs? If you search for "CRLF" you find places like https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parsing-an-event-stream with verbiage like

> Lines must be separated by either a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, or a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character.

Perhaps something like:

> In displaying the message, instances of a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, or a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character are equivalent in the effect of breaking a line

or something like this. And maybe even a non-normative example?

> [Example] A call like
> `alert("First line\rSecond line\r\nThird line\nFourth line")`
> will result in a dialog:
> ```
> First line
> Second line
> Third line
> Fourth line
> ```

@domenic Can you help?
